Position of the majority of young [sex of FGD] on the ladder of power and freedom (private rating): 5 = Power and freedom to make almost all major life decisions: 0 votes; 4 = Power and freedom to make many major life decisions: 5 votes; 3 = Power and freedom to make some major life decisions: 2 votes; 2 = Only a small amount of power and freedom: 3 votes; 1 = Almost no power or freedom to make decisions: 0 votes

We are unable to make all decisions because we are still children who are still looked after by parents. Thus what I want may be different from the rules of the house, for example, I may not want to go to my parent’s church but have I no choice but to go with them; I have clothes that I want to wear but I am not allowed.
To make all the decisions as a child/wife is difficult. Husband/parent cannot allow you to do that. Thus you have to listen to what they say. Though I can make some decisions.

Another reason is that as a child I may know what I am supposed to do thus though I have decisions that I can make I must listen to my parents. For example, I can choose the man I want to marry; I have greater decision power in this case though parents may discourage me, their power is less.
On many decisions a parent may request that I don’t go to school and I can dispute that. At times a parent may discourage me from working but is unable to buy me anything.
A parent cannot decide my future or what career path I should take. If they choose for me I may go against it.
If you are married you husband may allow you to make some decisions and not all. You have to listen to your husband since he is the head of household.
Sometimes parents can make decisions for us just because they may know what is dangerous for us and as children we may not know the danger involved in some of our decisions.
There is need to follow the laws and rules for each household. As children under our parents’ roof we have to listen to them.
If my parents are difficult to talk to I may not be able to make any decisions on my own.
As a young married woman you cannot make all independent decisions. You have to listen to your husband though you can make some small decisions.
I think that as the youth we are the leaders of tomorrow so education is very important for our future and also education allows good progress. The elders have fewer chances to uplift the country.
I think that if a child goes to school she will be able to make informed important life decisions. Some parents still think that a girl should not go to school: but education = informed decisions.
If we are educated, we will be able to look after our parents well.
Without education you cannot even read simple notices like Women’s toilet/ Men’s Toilets.
Education uplifts you, your parents and the area you live in.
Education is good because it will give you a good future. So that you are able to read and write.
You can get a job even with a certificate even if you did not pass too well.
I am able to elevate other people in the area.
If I have an education I can read even instructions on seed packages.
Education is also good because I think it gives one so many choices in life, like whether one wants to look for a job or open her own company
Educated girls have also better chances of being married to good educated men
Educated young women can also earn respect from their husbands and relatives
Boys
(All) Generally they go up to Form 4 though some do not write the exam due to lack of money.
Very few proceed to ‘A’ level and do some courses
Others have the opportunity for vocational skills trainings
Girls
Most of the girls do not go up to Form 4. Most go up to Form 2 or 3. Getting to form 4 is rare in this community
Most become pregnant before reaching Form 4.
Most of the churches are Mapostori Sects which encourages early marriages.
Boys
Boys should be more educated because if they are not educated they end up committing crime in the village.
They should go up to university level because they are the leaders more than women so that they may uplift the area.
For girls it is difficult because if you sleep with a boy you get pregnant but a guy can sleep with many girls and proceed to university
They should go beyond education so that they may teach other younger children and uneducated parents.
Boys must be educated until university and secure good jobs so that they can also take the youth from XX and offer them jobs
Boys should be educated until university level because education opens and sharpens one mind so with education we know we will have better husbands who knows how to treat a wife
Girls
Must go up to university and beyond; we know that it is possible because our Vice President and many other women have been educated to such levels.
A girl child should learn the same as boys because this life and jobs does not discriminate between men and women, so as boys go upto university level, so should also the girls.
An educated woman will always earn respect in her community, beyond her community and even among her own relatives
People will always listen to you if suggest anything when you are educated
Girls should be highly educated so that they may have their own businesses
Education also gives girls high self-esteem
When educated, a girl can choose a life-partner well and will not hesitate vto ask the guy to go for HIV testing before marriage

Parents say that girls should not be that educated because they will get married and all is lost to marriage. They strive for boys to get an education because they say these are the heads of households of tomorrow.
Parents do not show same commitment because most girls elope whilst they are still in school. This makes parents lose hope in girls.
Parents say that once a girl writes form 4 that’s it because girls do not bring wealth to the family. She will prosper the family she will get married to and not her own family.
I think it depends with the zeal/passion of the child, if the child doesn’t have the zeal they would rather educate a dull boy than a girl without passion for school.
Parents pay fees depending on how girls behave; for well behaved girls they show commitment, but if a girl has bad behavior the parents will not educate her further than Grade 7 or Form 2.
Some religious practices do not support educating a girl child instead they encourage that girls should get married once they reach puberty

Our church encourages girls to go to school but it depends on the parents if they do not want to send their own children to school. For example, if a girl is still in school and there is an old man who wants to marry the parents may give this child away.
Some parents want to educate their children but lack money.
My parents give both boys and girls same opportunities but the girls in my family elope before they even reach Form 4.
We were taught weeding the fields using a hoe when we were still young
Also taught how to plant maize seeds
I have heard of zero tillage but I really do not know how it works. I just know you make holes in a straight line and put grass to cover the ground between the lines.
I know about mulching using grass, maize stalks or groundnuts shells. This conserves moisture in the soil so that crops do not dry fast when there is less rain.
Putting manure – if you make lines and put manure this feeds maize in the event that you do not have fertilizer or may get it late.
Just making lines and planting without turning/disturbing the soil.
We also learnt about new maize seeds which have chemicals to help it resist various diseases.

I know that different maize seed varieties have different farming times, that is there are maize seeds which mature early and others mature late but I do not remember the names of these maize seed varieties
There are long season varieties which depend on the season and also short season varieties. That is the principles of conservation agriculture. You must know when to plant.
Zero tillage assist in the controlling of weeds through mulching the fields.
If we do zero tillage some weeds will not germinate because the soil will remain compact.

I learnt about forest conservation, for example using alternative sources of fuel like paraffin, gas, electricity, coal; this helps to conserve our forests. People used to cut trees to cure tobacco and burn bricks.
I learnt that I should plant across the slope and not along the slope to avoid soil erosion.
Build pens for goats during rainy seasons and spray the pens to control worm infestation.
I learnt about crop rotation, for example planting groundnuts then maize the next season
I learnt of planting potatoes in sacks
Catching fish using nets destroys the aquatic lives and removes other things which should stay in the water.
When doing laundry in the river you must not let soapy water into the river because it may cause the rivers to dry up.

Adding manure/fertilizers to seeds so that they are healthy
Conserving moisture in the soil through mulching
Not burn forests because this destroys pastures for our livestock, wild fruit trees and other small forest animals

Legume crops – we should put Rhisobium this stimulate the growth of nodules and nitrogen. When we now plant maize, it won’t need too much fertilizer because the nitrogen is already there in the soils.
If we harvest maize, we should put the stalks in the cattle pen as feed with a little bit of salt added
We should prevent post-harvest losses by making sure that the rooms where we keep the harvests are treated so as to keep away insects and pests.

Conservation agriculture

Yes agricultural practices have changed over the past ten years and I think this is mainly because of the discoveries of other new farming practices, for example ten years ago it was common for all household to use ox-drawn ploughs in their fields but now the basins have taken over and have better advantages than the old practices
I also think that the discovery of new farming machineries like the direct seeder has enabled people to change their farming methods since such machines are quick to use, saves time and labor
The willingness of people to learn and adapt to new farming methods has caused changes in agricultural practices

It has always been our custom that a woman should have a granary/stock of groundnuts because this is where her money comes from. Even now it is still common that women prefer groundnuts because it gives them freedom to do as they wish with the crop.

It is still common to find that even young men today are mostly the ones that prepare the fields with an ox-drawn ploughs because somehow this requires a lot of strength and men by their make-up are stronger physically

Gardens have always been common with women since years back and this is because women are mainly responsible for feeding the families, so as a woman you do not want your children to starve when you can produce vegetables in the gardens

Other customs that are still practiced by women in agriculture are weeding the fields, planting seeds, winnowing grains during harvest. The main reason why women are still practicing these activities I think it is because we saw our mothers doing it and to us it is the norm

Common customs that are still practiced by men in agriculture are ploughing, cultivating, land clearing on new plot, shelling and treating maize, sewing maize sacks and storing them, spraying the field, ensuring security in the granary. Also I think men have continued with these activities because it has always been the norm
I think generally men will struggle with growing groundnuts for example because it needs a lot of patience and with men not being so patient I think they will easily give up

Even harvesting groundnuts, most men do not like the processes of harvesting and always think women are kind of wasting time when harvesting so I think men will also struggle during harvesting of groundnuts
Men not even the familiar with the good groundnuts seed varieties that are good for our soils, so he may plant a variety that will not give him a good harvest

Selling of groundnuts processed goods like peanut butter, roasted peanuts may not be easy for men since most women go to sell at the market place which is dominated by women, a man may fail to fit into this market
However, those men that know a lot about groundnuts from their wives and usually help their wives in the groundnuts field may not struggle at all to grow and sell the groundnuts

For example if a young woman tried to raise or keep cattle I think she may face difficulties in making sure that every day the cattle are taken out for grazing yet she may also need to make sure that she has done all household chores
Even there at the grazing places, it is not a place for women, one may even risk being raped there or even insulted
A woman may not have a full appreciation of all the medicines and injections that are important for the survival of the cattle
A woman may also not know other indigenous systems of raising cattle that men were taught when they were boys by their elders so she may struggle with raising cattle

Selling of cattle may be difficult because once other buyers see that it is a woman selling they may actually take advantage of her in terms of offering the buying price and the woman may not have good negotiating skills on the pricing

In general the father/husband is the one who decides who should plant on a particular piece of land, mainly the father gives the mother a plot to grow her own crops like groundnuts, roundnuts and cow peas. However though other plots may be referred to as ‘the father’s’ these are also the family/household plots
Usually the father chooses the fields that are still very fertile as household plots and gives the wife those plots that are less fertile
A young girl cannot be given a piece of land to own/plant, she is expected to help in the family fields

A young man may be given a piece of land. It depends on the family’s land size whether they give him a big/small piece. Some are given a piece of land when they marry so that they can grow food for their families

Sometimes young men even younger than the girls may be given land but not the girls because they shall marry and get land in their new home and most fathers always look at the boy child as head of household who must be groomed accordingly
A woman may get a separate plot to plant groundnuts but it is very rare to find a husband helping in her wife’s field though there are very few men who does help here and there.
Very few husbands who have come to a realization that groundnuts is also a cash crop are now helping their wives because they also want to be given some few dollars for beer
Men have always had this mindset that growing of groundnuts is not serious business but they view it more as a hobby
Women Helping

Women do work a lot on their husbands’ or family plots because if the man gives directives that everyone must go work in those fields, no one can dispute this because the moment as a wife you want to dispute a man can even take away that field he had allocated to you for your own crops, so as women we comply
Other women work in the husbands’ maize plots because they know that is where food for the family is grown and no one wants their children to starve
During harvesting of maize, women also work under instruction from their husbands because most men fear post harvest losses so they always want to make sure that they harvest maize well on time
Some men will only allow their wives to work in their own fields of groundnuts when most work is complete in the household plot, men prioritize food security for the families
Even during preparation of the maize fields, most men give directives to their wives to prepare the land whilst some men never even come to help to prepare land especially if using basins
A married woman will discuss issues about hiring extra labor with her husband and they can both agree on the work to be done and how they will pay the laborers

Extra labor is easily available around villages, people know who is available to provide extra labor so one needs extra labor it is a matter of approaching such people and these are paid with cash or food or second hand clothes

[Do women have other responsibilities that sometimes interfere with farming responsibilities?] Yes, sickness in the family can hinder a woman from carrying out farming activities since it is common that it a woman who takes care of the sick
Daily household chores like fetching water and firewood may result in a woman failing to go to fields because the body would be tired
Other women that are in full time employment may fail to always be in the fields
A woman may decide to go and work for food for her children especially if there is nothing to eat in the house thereby abandoning field work
Even going to sell at the market to get money to buy food for the family hinder sone from doing field work

[In general, is the right kind of labor available for agricultural activities when needed?] Yes labor is always available throughout different season, as mentioned earlier people know those that are available to work for food, seeds, fertilizers and second hand clothes, so we approach these people whenever we need extra labor

[How do women obtain additional labor when needed - in or outside the household?] For married women it is matter of discussing and agreeing with the husband on the work that needs extra labor and how much to pay these people then approach those we already know are readily available
Other women work in co-operatives or groups where they rotate field work for all their members, this way one is guaranteed of getting extra labor
Some may even ask their friends to come and help them and in turn they also go and help in their friends’ fields
How do female-headed households go about obtaining adult male labor when they need it during the rainy season?]

A woman may brew beer and spread a word around to men to come and help with work in the fields, after the work is done, men can drink beer and eat some food –this is their payment beer and cooked food to eat

Other women who have ploughs and cattle, may ask their friends with husbands to come and help them cultivating their fields and once they are down, the woman also gives her friends her ploughs and cattle to go work in their fields as a way of paying them
Some women may obtain male labor from their churches to come and help and must pay either in cash or food or seeds
Some may get assistance from their children or their husbands’ relatives, depending on how good their relationships are
